expectations.evidence: Full hierarchy with named tenants (tn-bu1-engineering..tn-bu5-research, tn-shared-services, tn-dmz, tn-infra-openstack), VRFs (vrf-bu1..vrf-bu5, vrf-shared, vrf-dmz), BDs (bd-bu1-web/app/db per BU with subnets), EPGs (epg-bu1-web/app/db per BU) all explicitly named in sections 3.1-3.5.

expectations.text: epg_contract_design(specific Contracts between specific EPGs with Filters)
expectations.evidence: Section 3.4 defines specific contracts (ctr-bu1-web-to-app, ctr-bu1-app-to-db, ctr-internet-to-dmz, ctr-dmz-to-web, ctr-shared-services) with explicit provider/consumer EPGs, named filters (flt-allow-web TCP 80/443, flt-allow-app TCP 8080/8443, flt-allow-db TCP 3306/5432, etc.), and scopes.

Section 4 details cisco_apic_ml2 mechanism driver, OpFlex mode with opflex-agent on compute nodes, and explicit mapping table: Neutron Network→EPG, Subnet→BD Subnet, Router→VRF, Security Group→Contract+Filters. Neutron config shown with ml2_conf.ini specifying type_drivers=opflex and mechanism_drivers=cisco_apic_ml2.

Section 5.1 defines sg-paloalto-fw service graph template with PBR enabled, L4-L7 device cluster dc-paloalto (Virtual, FW type), function node N1-firewall (GoTo with redirect), PBR policies pbr-paloalto-outside/inside with specific IPs (198.51.100.10, 10.250.0.10) and health groups.

expectations.text: service_graph_loadbalancer(ACI SG or Octavia for LB)
expectations.evidence: Section 5.2 defines sg-f5-lb service graph template with PBR, L4-L7 device cluster dc-f5-bigip (Virtual, ADC type, multi-context), function node N1-loadbalancer with GoTo/redirect. Also mentions Octavia/HAProxy available as self-service option for non-production.

Section 5.2.1 has explicit comparison table: F5 has native ACI SG integration, iRules/WAF/SSL offload, route domains, ACI PBR support but higher operational complexity; HAProxy/Octavia has no L4-L7 device support, basic L7, resource-heavy amphora, but lower complexity. Decision justified.

expectations.text: shared_services_design(vzAny,shared L3Out,or shared VRF for DNS/LDAP/monitoring)
expectations.evidence: Section 3.4.2-3.4.3 describes tn-shared-services with vrf-shared, epg-dns/epg-ldap/epg-monitoring providing ctr-shared-services contract (global scope). vzAny in each vrf-buN consumes this contract. BD subnet 10.200.0.0/24 marked shared. Inter-VRF route leaking via contract export/import.

Each BU gets its own VRF (vrf-bu1..vrf-bu5). Section 6.4 explicitly shows inter-BU isolation: BU1→BU2 traffic dropped because no contract exists between vrf-bu1 and vrf-bu2, no routes leaked. Section 10.2 enforcement matrix confirms BU1→BU2 DENIED by VRF isolation.

Section 6.1 provides 10-step flow: Internet→Border Leaf (ext-epg-internet)→PBR to PAN outside (198.51.100.10)→PAN inspects untrust→trust, DNAT to F5 VIP→PBR to F5→F5 selects pool member→inter-VRF routing→compute leaf→epg-bu1-web endpoint via opflex-agent.

Section 8 covers: Terraform with CiscoDevNet/aci provider (full HCL for tenants, SGs, PBR in 8.2-8.3), Ansible for OpenStack deployment and PAN config via paloaltonetworks.panos collection (8.4-8.5), F5 AS3 JSON declaration (8.6), plus GitLab CI/CD pipeline and Python day-2 automation script.

Section 14.2 defines l3out-internet in tn-dmz/vrf-dmz with BGP peering: peer IP 203.0.113.1, remote AS 65100, local AS 65000, keepalive 10/hold 30, route maps for inbound/outbound. External EPG ext-epg-internet with subnet 0.0.0.0/0 (external-subnets, shared-security, shared-rtctrl).

Section 8.5 configures zones (untrust, trust, dmz), interfaces mapped to zones, security rule 'allow-https-inbound' from untrust→trust with application=['ssl','web-browsing'] (App-ID), log_end enabled. NAT rule for DNAT web-to-f5 with source/destination zones and specific IPs. Managed via Panorama device group.
